cards.d: If something is astronomical, then it is extremely large.
cards.e: It’s an astronomical distance between the Milky Way galaxy and the nearest galaxy.
cards.ielts: Property prices in London have reached astronomical levels, making it almost impossible for young people to buy a home.

cards.d: An atom is the smallest unit of a substance.
cards.e: A molecule consists of a combination of two or more atoms.
cards.ielts: Nuclear power stations generate electricity by splitting atoms, a process that produces very little carbon dioxide.

cards.d: Breadth is the distance from one side to the other side of something.
cards.e: The breadth of the northern wall of the house is twenty meters.
cards.ielts: The breadth of the new motorway allows six lanes of traffic, but critics say it has divided the community in two.

cards.d: A circumference is the distance completely around a circular object.
cards.e: The circumference of the Earth is obviously much larger than a baseball’s.
cards.ielts: The new cycle path runs around the entire circumference of the lake, attracting thousands of visitors every weekend.

cards.d: A comet is an object in space made of ice and rock with a tail of glowing dust.
cards.e: Comets take many decades to complete an orbit around a star.
cards.ielts: Space agencies have spent billions sending probes to study comets, but some argue the money should be spent on problems on Earth.

cards.d: A crater is a large hole in a planet’s or moon’s surface.
cards.e: They could clearly see the big crater on the moon through the telescope.
cards.ielts: Scientists believe that a huge crater in Mexico was formed by the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs.

cards.d: A crescent is the curved shape lit on the moon’s face during its early and late stages.
cards.e: Ten days ago the entire moon was bright, but now only a small crescent is shining.
cards.ielts: The crescent of the new moon marks the beginning of Ramadan, a month of fasting for Muslims all over the world.

cards.d: Debris is the small pieces scattered from something wrecked or destroyed.
cards.e: The debris from the cube scattered on the floor.
cards.ielts: Thousands of pieces of space debris now orbit the Earth, posing a serious danger to satellites and astronauts.

cards.d: Despair is the complete loss of hope.
cards.e: After the other company won the account, our salespeople were filled with despair.
cards.ielts: Long-term unemployment can lead to feelings of despair, especially among young people who see no future for themselves.

cards.d: To embed something means to place it firmly within a surrounding thing.
cards.e: The logger embedded the ax into the wood after chopping several logs.
cards.ielts: Digital skills should be embedded in every school subject rather than taught only in separate computer lessons.

cards.d: A fragment is a small part of something.
cards.e: After the light broke, there were fragments of glass to clean up.
cards.ielts: Archaeologists discovered fragments of pottery suggesting that people lived in the area more than three thousand years ago.

cards.d: A galaxy is any extremely large collection of star systems.
cards.e: Our solar system is located in the outer area of our galaxy.
cards.ielts: Powerful new telescopes allow astronomers to observe galaxies that formed shortly after the birth of the universe.

cards.d: If something is gigantic, then it is extremely large.
cards.e: Some dinosaurs were so gigantic that they were the size of buildings.
cards.ielts: Gigantic container ships carry most of the world’s goods, making globalisation possible but also polluting the oceans.

cards.d: Gloom is a state of being almost completely dark.
cards.e: In the gloom of the morning, it was difficult to see the boat on the lake.
cards.ielts: In northern countries, the long winter gloom can affect people’s mood, which is why some doctors recommend light therapy.

cards.d: To radiate means to send out energy or heat.
cards.e: The heat from the fireplace radiated throughout the room.
cards.ielts: Dark roofs absorb sunlight and radiate heat, which is one reason why city centres are often warmer than the countryside.

cards.d: To roam means to move around without a plan or purpose.
cards.e: All day the cows roamed around the field eating grass.
cards.ielts: In some cities, stray dogs roam the streets freely, which can be dangerous for children and elderly people.

cards.d: If something is solitary, then it is lonely or the only one.
cards.e: The only thing in the room was a solitary chair.
cards.ielts: Working from home can become a solitary experience, so employees should make an effort to stay in contact with colleagues.

cards.d: The spectrum is the full range of color ranging from red to violet.
cards.e: You can see the entire spectrum in a rainbow.
cards.ielts: Solar panels convert light from the visible spectrum into electricity, but scientists are developing models that use infrared light too.

cards.d: A sphere is a three-dimensional round shape, like a ball.
cards.e: The balloons were inflated into a variety of colorful spheres.
cards.ielts: The new science museum is housed in a huge glass sphere that has become one of the city’s most famous landmarks.

cards.d: Status is the position of something or someone in relation to others.
cards.e: She had achieved the status of being the smartest girl in the class.
cards.ielts: In many societies, owning an expensive car is still seen as a symbol of high social status.
